findings.title: Theorem 1.6 admits driftless finite-activity subordinators without the required Green density
operative_hypotheses: Levy density mu with integral (1 wedge s) mu(s) finite
Independent Brownian motion on R^d; application with Lebesgue reference measure; choose bounded open ball D
findings.evidence: b=0, mu(s)=exp(-s); integral mu=1, integral(1 wedge s)mu=1-exp(-1), phi(lambda)=lambda/(1+lambda), c=exp(8) satisfies both inequalities. S is rate-one compound Poisson with exponential jumps. P_x(X_t=x)=exp(-t), G^alpha(x,{x})=1/(alpha+1). For any open U containing x, expected killed occupation of {x} is E T1=1, whereas a Lebesgue occupation density integrates to zero on {x}.
findings.core_dependency: The universal density assertion supplies (A1) needed by Corollary 1.5 for the stated Theorem 1.6 application; for the admitted example Definition 1.1 Green density does not exist.
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: Discontinuous does not exclude compound Poisson; b>=0 is explicit.
Density is completely monotone, so complete Bernstein reinterpretation does not exclude example.
Section 3's positive-drift restriction is local; p.29 explicitly extends (A3)' beyond positive drift but does not repair (A1).
Removing the diagonal atom changes Definition 1.1; cannot represent all bounded Borel test functions.
Theorem 1.3 assumes A1 and Theorem 1.10 explicitly b>0; neither is refuted.
findings.repair: Add an explicit needed absolute-continuity hypothesis, or exclude driftless finite-activity subordinators. b>0 or infinite activity removes this atom; this alone does not independently verify every other assumption or transition-density continuity.
findings.impact: False universal density assertion and invalid application/undefined Green formulation on the full stated class. No counterexample to the BHP inequality itself; no whole-paper theorem-falsity claim.
findings.reviewed_version_limit: Exact acquired arXiv v1 only; publisher VoR unavailable for comparison.

findings.title: Lemma 4.1 separates coordinate maxima in a false equality
locators: p.44 Lemma 4.1 and definitions of K,G,L
operative_hypotheses: Arbitrary Levy process in R^d, positive semidefinite covariance A, legitimate Levy measure nu and drift
findings.evidence: Define B_i=int_{|z|<=2r} z_i^2 nu(dz). The joint maximum M=max_i(a_ii/2+c2 B_i) is replaced by (max_i a_ii)/2+c2 max_i B_i. For d=2,r=1,A=diag(1/2,0),zero drift,nu=(delta_(0,1)+delta_(0,-1))/2,c2=1/4: B=(0,1),K(2r)=3/8,G=L=0; M=1/4 but separated sum=1/2. Valid cosine constant since 1-cos u>=u^2/4 on |u|<=1. Parametric example A=diag(2c2,0) works for any c2>0.
findings.core_dependency: Case (i) yields C/sqrt(tK(2r)) then independent increments gives C/(tPhi(2r)); Lemma 4.1 supports Theorem 2.8 and A4 in Theorem 2.9.
findings.repair: Keep joint M and use M >= d^-1 sum_i(a_ii/2+c2 B_i) >= min(1/2,c2)/d*(tr A+sum_i B_i)=min(1/2,c2)/d*4r^2K(2r). Same Gaussian integral rate follows.
alternate_readings_and_counterevidence: Both maxima need not occur at the same coordinate; an isotropic special case would not justify arbitrary Levy triples.
The final estimate is locally repairable with the same order; no counterexample to Lemma 4.1 or Pruitt's final theorem.
findings.impact: Demonstrated intermediate algebraic error, repaired in full locally; final theorem not refuted.
